calls.head: Lohrei and Brunet get the Michkov assignment
calls.body: At home, the Bruins keep sending Lohrei and Brunet out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Marco Sturm has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ third lines. Tonight the Flyers’ third line is Foerster, Barkey and Michkov.

calls.head: Where the Flyers have the edge: shots from in close
calls.body: The Flyers are around the middle of the league for shots from in close, and the Bruins are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Bruins roll past the Flyers
paras: Pavel Zacha opened the scoring for the Bruins midway through the first. Mason Lohrei and Marat Khusnutdinov scored 4:43 apart late in the second to stretch the lead to 3-0. Porter Martone got the Flyers on the board on the power play 4:37 later. Casey Mittelstadt stretched the lead to 4-1, 2:49 later. Fraser Minten made it 5-1 with 4:01 left. Minten finished with a goal and two assists.
The Bruins carried the play, outshooting the Flyers 32-15, and got the result to match. Jeremy Swayman made 14 saves for the Bruins, and Dan Vladař allowed five goals on 32 shots.
Minten and Martone picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Bruins moved to 4-2-0.

items.text: The Flyers are 0-4-2, still looking for their first win.
Pavel Zacha scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 7.
